name: Ebbs
kurzbeschreibung: Border town near the German border featuring the Kleinholz pilgrimage church and a shopping center right on the edge of Kufstein.
beschreibung:
Overview

Ebbs lies at an altitude of 475 meters in the Lower Inn Valley within the Untere Schranne region, right on the border with Bavaria. Home to around 5,800 inhabitants, the vibrant village nestles against the dramatic limestone backdrop of the Zahmer Kaiser massif. Renowned worldwide as the cradle and capital of purebred Haflinger horses, Ebbs features traditional alpine farmsteads, blooming gardens, and lush pastures. Serving as the northern gateway to the Kaisergebirge nature reserve, the village harmoniously combines rural charm with diverse recreational activities for hikers, families, and nature enthusiasts.

History

Traces of human presence in the area date back into deep prehistory, as evidenced by archaeological finds from around 30,000 BC in nearby Tischofer Cave. Ebbs was first documented in 788 AD in the Salzburg diocesan register Indiculus Arnonis under the name Episas, which recorded two churches with extensive estates. The name likely derives from the Celtic word for horse stream, echoing a centuries-old equine heritage. For generations, Ebbs served as the ancient mother parish of the entire lower valley. The magnificent Parish Church of the Assumption, popularly hailed as the Cathedral of the Lower Inn Valley, was constructed between 1748 and 1756 by Bavarian master builder Abraham Millauer. Inside, visitors admire expansive ceiling frescoes by Joseph Adam Ritter von Mölck and an ornate high altar enshrining a Late Gothic wooden Madonna from around 1450. In 1947, the establishment of the Fohlenhof Ebbs stud farm founded the town's international reputation as the global headquarters of the Haflinger breed.

Getting There

By car, Ebbs is reached easily from Germany via the motorway A93 toll-free from the Oberaudorf or Kiefersfelden exits within minutes. Travelers from Innsbruck or Salzburg take motorway A12 to the Kufstein Nord exit and follow road B175 for approximately six kilometers into the village center. Train passengers arrive at the major transport hub Kufstein railway station, served by international Railjet, Eurocity, and regional trains. From the station forecourt, VVT regional bus lines 4030 and 4036 depart frequently, reaching Ebbs in just twelve minutes. With the local KufsteinerlandCard guest card, regional bus travel is complimentary for overnight visitors.

Tips

A tour of the historic Fohlenhof Ebbs stud farm is essential, featuring daily stables visits, an equine museum, and lively equestrian demonstrations in summer. Families enjoy the private Ebbs Rarity Zoo at the base of the mountains, housing over 500 exotic animals. Hiking enthusiasts can conquer the Kaiseraufstieg with its 300 steps leading into the tranquil, car-free Kaisertal nature reserve or embark on summits like Pyramidenspitze. A culinary stop at Aschinger Alm showcases artisanal alpine cheese alongside splendid panoramic vistas across the Wilder and Zahmer Kaiser mountains.
